question: Why ephemeral after-flush peak ~495 MB vs live scoped peak 2539.6 MB (flush-25)?

ephemeralAfterScoped.database: empty ephemeral Postgres + synthetic seed only

liveFlush25.database: Railway production Postgres via event-os internal network

finding.dominantCause: Unscoped platform_documents already hydrated into the live installer process (production corpus). Each mutate()/replace() double-clones that full in-memory graph; pending flush queues retain prior clones. Ephemeral DB never contained production document volume (after.seed 170.7 MiB vs live 823.1 MiB). Raw SQL grand size remains ~29.8 MiB — not a two-order-of-magnitude explanation by itself; V8 object-graph + multi-clone retention is.
finding.growthAcrossInstall: Live RSS jumps from before.guests 596.7 MiB to 2022.3 MiB by the first guest flush window (25 guests under flush-25), then peaks at 2539.6 MiB near guest 525 — cost grows during guest mutation windows, not only at initial hydrate.
finding.phase1SecondaryFlag: Yes — platform_documents (largest share of serialized bytes; operationalGuests now 5.565 MiB / 3995 rows) is the unscoped production mass ephemeral lacked.
finding.flushCadenceLever: Flush-5 completed peak 1506.4 MiB vs flush-25 peak 2539.6 MiB (delta 1033.2 MiB, 40.7% lower). Layer A remains a real lever on production-sized state, but does not close the gap to ephemeral (~495 MiB).

furtherScopingProposal.expectedNewPeak: Not measured; do not claim without a scoped-documents run
